title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: Officers, full-time, part-time and casual employees, contractors, consultants, secondees and advisers of Woodside group companies who are not directors or restricted employees. May deal at any time without notifying Woodside provided they hold no inside information, pass the Front Page Test and are not short-term or speculative dealing; subject to plan rules.

tiers.name: directors
tiers.description: Directors of Woodside Energy Group Ltd including the CEO. Subject to black-out periods, prior written approval with a Compliance Certificate, the derivatives and hedging bans, the pledging ban, minimum shareholding requirements and immediate post-trade reporting for ASX filing.

tiers.name: restricted employees
tiers.description: Direct reports to the CEO (including all executive key management personnel), the Company Secretary/ies, and employees nominated by the Group General Counsel for access to inside information; the GGC maintains the list. Subject to black-out periods and Compliance Certificate acknowledgement by the GGC before dealing. CEO direct reports and Company Secretaries are also within the pledging ban.

tiers.name: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
tiers.description: The tier subject to section 5: prohibited from hedging unvested or holding-locked entitlements and from any transaction in Woodside-based derivative securities, including collars and writing puts or calls, whether for hedging purposes or not.

tiers.name: family members and controlled entities
tiers.description: Spouse, partner, child or other immediate family member, or trust or other entity controlled by a director or restricted employee, and investment advisers acting for any of them. The director or restricted employee must follow the section 6.2 process for their intended dealings and take reasonable steps to prevent the trade until acknowledged or approved. The Policy also extends to all securities owned or controlled through a company, trust, family member, friend or other arrangement.

definitions.hedging_definition: any transaction which would have the effect of hedging, or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of, any unvested entitlement in Woodside securities or vested Woodside securities that remain subject to a holding lock or similar restriction under a Woodside equity incentive plan

windows.start_anchor: end of Woodside's financial year (31 December)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement or public disclosure of Woodside's full year results

windows.start_anchor: end of Woodside's half year (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement or public disclosure of Woodside's half year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CEO may declare other black-out periods from time to time; the Group General Counsel may nominate employees as restricted employees because of project or transaction work. The policy does not say whether declared black-out periods are confidential, but a refusal of clearance, approval or acknowledgement must be kept confidential.

rules.tier: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions in Woodside-based derivative securities (options, warrants, stock appreciation rights, convertible notes or similar rights), whether or not for hedging, expressly including option contracts, straddles or collars and writing puts or calls, plus debt convertible into Woodside shares. Holding, exercising or settling plan awards is carved out.
rules.evidence: Transactions in derivative securities include, but are not limited to: trading in Woodside-based option contracts; transactions in straddles or collars; and/or writing puts or calls.

rules.detail: For restricted employees outside the section 5 tier (e.g. GGC-nominated employees not in an executive incentive plan), third-party derivatives over Woodside shares are securities and granting, accepting or acquiring an option is a dealing, so a Compliance Certificate must be acknowledged by the Group General Counsel and the dealing completed within 7 days, outside black-out periods; the requirement is stated expressly for products limiting the economic risk of a vested holding.
rules.evidence: These requirements also apply to dealings in financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Woodside securities.

rules.detail: Employees may deal in derivatives over Woodside securities at any time without notification, subject to holding no inside information, the Front Page Test and the ban on short-term or speculative dealing, which in practice constrains short-dated or speculative option positions.
rules.evidence: you can deal in Woodside securities at any time provided you do not have inside information, the proposed dealing would pass the Front Page Test and you are not involved in short term or speculative dealing

rules.tier: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
rules.detail: No transaction may hedge or transfer to another person the risk of fluctuation in the value of an unvested entitlement.
rules.evidence: are prohibited from entering into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging, or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of, any unvested entitlement in Woodside securities

rules.tier: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
rules.detail: The hedging ban extends to vested securities still subject to a holding lock or similar plan restriction.
rules.evidence: or vested Woodside securities that remain subject to a holding lock or similar restriction under a Woodside equity incentive plan.

rules.tier: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unlocked shares is not itself banned for this tier, but every practical hedge (collar, purchased put, written call, swap-like right) is a transaction in Woodside-based derivative securities, which section 5.1 prohibits 'whether entered into for hedging purposes or not'.
rules.evidence: Transactions involving Woodside-based derivative securities by directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan, are also prohibited.

rules.detail: Restricted employees outside the section 5 tier may enter third-party financial products limiting the economic risk of a vested holding, subject to Compliance Certificate acknowledgement by the Group General Counsel, the 7-day window, black-out periods and the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: These requirements also apply to dealings in financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Woodside securities.

rules.detail: Employees outside section 5 are not restricted from hedging vested, unlocked holdings beyond the general insider trading, Front Page Test, short-term dealing and plan rules; the Policy applies to subsequent dealings in plan securities.
rules.evidence: This Policy does not restrict participation in Woodside employee share and equity incentive plans but does apply in respect of any subsequent dealing in Woodside securities to which you become entitled under those plans.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or funded collar is a transaction in derivative securities banned by 5.1, and any structure secured on the shares is pledging banned by 8.1.
rules.evidence: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: For CEO direct reports and Company Secretaries, any secured monetisation is pledging banned by 8.1, and executive plan participants are also within the 5.1 derivatives ban. A GGC-nominated restricted employee outside both bans could monetise only as a dealing requiring Compliance Certificate acknowledgement.
rules.evidence: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: Short selling is named as a form of short-term or speculative dealing and banned for everyone covered by the Policy, directly or indirectly.
rules.evidence: It is Woodside's policy that you must not engage, directly or indirectly, in short-term or speculative dealing (including short-selling) in Woodside securities.

rules.detail: Lending securities is not named; borrowing appears only in the description of short selling. A loan of shares would likely be a dealing under the broad 'any transaction or change affecting title to, or interest in, securities' chapeau but the Policy does not address it.

rules.tier: directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a 'similar right whose value is derived from the value of an equity security' and so a Woodside-based derivative security banned for this tier; it would also be speculative dealing under 3.1.
rules.evidence: 'Derivative securities' are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights, convertible notes or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security.

rules.detail: For restricted employees outside the section 5 tier a CFD is a third-party financial product in relation to Woodside shares requiring Compliance Certificate acknowledgement, and would be caught by the speculative dealing ban if used for short-term trading.
rules.evidence: derivatives (such as exchange-traded options and warrants) and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside shares, debentures and options

rules.detail: Directors may not pledge Woodside securities as collateral, expressly including shares held in a margin account, because a foreclosure sale while aware of inside information may be unlawful insider trading.
rules.evidence: Woodside securities pledged as collateral, including shares held in a margin account, may be sold without your consent by the lender in foreclosure if you default on your loan.

rules.detail: The pledging ban covers Company Secretaries and direct reports to the CEO but not GGC-nominated restricted employees, for whom a margin loan is a dealing (granting a charge) requiring Compliance Certificate acknowledgement and subject to the 3.1 three-month rule.
rules.evidence: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: Employees are not barred from margin loans but must not enter arrangements such as margin loans that could result in securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition; section 8.1 warns of insider trading risk on foreclosure.
rules.evidence: If you acquire Woodside securities, you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.

rules.detail: Pledging Woodside securities as collateral in any form is banned for directors; using securities as security or granting a charge or encumbrance is also a dealing under 2.3.
rules.evidence: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: Banned for Company Secretaries and CEO direct reports. Other restricted employees may grant a charge or encumbrance only as a dealing with Compliance Certificate acknowledgement.
rules.evidence: using as security or otherwise granting a charge or encumbrance over securities

rules.detail: Granting a charge is a dealing; employees may do so subject to the general rules and no notification is required.
rules.evidence: using as security or otherwise granting a charge or encumbrance over securities

rules.detail: Any borrowing secured by a pledge of Woodside securities is prohibited for directors with no approval route; the section 4.3 exceptional circumstances clearance permits disposals only.
rules.evidence: Due to this risk, directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: Prohibited for Company Secretaries and direct reports to the CEO. GGC-nominated restricted employees outside that group are not within the ban and would treat a secured loan as a dealing requiring acknowledgement.
rules.evidence: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

rules.detail: Not prohibited for employees, subject to the three-month disposal rule for arrangements that could force a sale of recently acquired securities and the insider trading warning in 8.1.
rules.evidence: Employees can risk breaching insider trading laws if they enter borrowing arrangements that may result in the sale of securities at the time they possess inside information.

rules.detail: Three-month minimum holding period from acquisition, extended to arrangements (such as margin loans) that could result in disposal within that period; sales of plan securities are carved out. The section 4.3 exceptional circumstances clearance can override it for disposals.
rules.evidence: If you acquire Woodside securities, you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board (CEO in the case of the Chair) and the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee, sought by the Group Company Secretary after consulting the Disclosure Committee or its Chair; approvers who are themselves dealing must delegate
clearance.post_trade_to: Group Company Secretary (sufficient details for ASX notice within 5 business days)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Any such approval will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given, meaning the relevant dealing can only occur during that period (subject to the other requirements of this Policy) ... A response would normally be expected within 24 hours

clearance.approver: Direct manager, then the Group General Counsel for acknowledgement of the Compliance Certificate (acknowledgement may be refused, conditioned or revoked)
clearance.post_trade_to: Group General Counsel (confirmation of any dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: the relevant dealing can only occur within the 7 days from the date of acknowledgement of the Compliance Certificate by the Group General Counsel
you are not required to notify Woodside if you intend to deal in Woodside securities or after you have dealt in such securities.

clearance.approver: Same process as the relevant director or restricted employee under 6.2, who must take reasonable steps to prevent the trade until acknowledged or approved
clearance.post_trade_to: Group Company Secretary (directors) or Group General Counsel (restricted employees)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Directors and restricted employees should follow the requirements outlined in Section 6.2 if they are aware that their spouse, partner, child or other immediate family member, or trust or other entity controlled by the director or restricted employee ... intends to deal in Woodside securities.

carve_outs: sale of securities acquired under Woodside's employee share and equity incentive plans
disposals cleared under section 4.3 in exceptional circumstances
short_term.evidence: If you acquire Woodside securities, you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.

exceptions.approver: Written application to the Group Company Secretary; approval by the Chair of the Board for directors, the CEO for the Chair, or the Group General Counsel for restricted employees
exceptions.evidence: a director or restricted employee who is not in possession of inside information may be given clearance to dispose of (but not acquire) Woodside securities where they would otherwise be restricted by this Policy if: they are in severe financial difficulty
the disposal is required under a court order

exceptions.approver: Board determines the exceptional circumstances; clearance under 4.3
exceptions.evidence: there are other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Board.

undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer; take up of entitlements under a rights issue or other offer; allowing entitlements to lapse under a rights issue or other offer; sale of entitlements under a rights issue
acquisitions under a dividend reinvestment plan where the election to participate in the plan and any variations to that participation were made in accordance with this Policy

exceptions.approver: Board approves the plan determining timing and structure
exceptions.evidence: dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a security purchase plan or equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

dealing where the beneficial interest in the Woodside securities does not change, including for example, the deposit of shares with the depositary in exchange for American Depositary Shares (ADSs) or the cancellation of ADSs and withdrawal of the underlying shares through the depositary
disposal of Woodside securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights

transfer of Woodside securities already held into a superannuation fund or other scheme in which the director or restricted employee is a beneficiary, provided the director or restricted employee (including an associate of the director or restricted employee) has no influence or control over the trustee

investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Woodside securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

exceptions.approver: Group General Counsel approval needed for restricted employees' elections or discretionary exercises during a black-out period; directors may not make elections or exercise rights in a black-out
exceptions.evidence: This Policy does not restrict participation in Woodside employee share and equity incentive plans but does apply in respect of any subsequent dealing in Woodside securities to which you become entitled under those plans.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Section 8.1 warns that a lender's foreclosure sale while the borrower is aware of inside information may be unlawful insider trading; no price-trigger or loan-to-value guidance is given.
financing_disclosure: directors: pre-dealing written request with Compliance Certificate to the Group Company Secretary; post-dealing details immediately (ideally same day) to the Group Company Secretary for ASX filing within 5 business days; granting a charge is a dealing.

restricted employees: Compliance Certificate to direct manager and Group General Counsel before dealing; confirmation to the Group General Counsel ideally by close of business on the day of the dealing.
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Section 6.2 refers to directors' and restricted employees' 'minimum shareholding requirements' as a separate constraint on dealing; the Policy does not say whether hedged or pledged shares count.

external_documents: Compliance Certificate form (Woodside intranet, Group Company Secretary or Group General Counsel)
Woodside equity-based incentive plan rules (holding locks and plan-specific dealing restrictions)
List of restricted employees maintained by the Group General Counsel
Minimum shareholding requirements for directors and restricted employees
exemption_authority: Under 4.3 the Chair of the Board (directors), the CEO (the Chair) or the Group General Counsel (restricted employees), on written application through the Group Company Secretary, may clear a disposal (never an acquisition) otherwise restricted by the Policy in severe financial difficulty, under a court order or in other exceptional circumstances determined by the Board; the clearance specifies its validity period and the approver must not be dealing at the time. No authority exists to waive the derivatives, hedging or pledging bans, and the section 7 exclusions do not apply to directors in black-out periods.
jurisdiction_overlays: US Securities Exchange Act of 1934 insider trading prohibition (NYSE listing); ADS deposit and withdrawal mechanics
ASX Listing Rules director notification within 5 business days

bespoke_clauses.clause: Transactions involving Woodside-based derivative securities by directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan, are also prohibited. ... Transactions in derivative securities include ... transactions in straddles or collars; and/or writing puts or calls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is expressly named as a prohibited transaction for directors and executive plan participants irrespective of hedging purpose or vesting state, so no approval route exists for the option legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently banned for directors and the executive team, but not for GGC-nominated restricted employees or ordinary employees.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exclusions carved back for directors in black-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to the insider trading prohibitions outlined above, and other than in relation to dealings by Directors in black-out periods, the following dealings by a director or restricted employee are excluded from the operation of this Policy: ... disposal of Woodside securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A secured lender's enforcement sale is outside the Policy for restricted employees, but for a director it would be a black-out period breach; the same carve-back applies to custodian or depositary transfers by directors in black-out.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging vested holdings by restricted employees
bespoke_clauses.clause: These requirements also apply to dealings in financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Woodside securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly contemplates restricted employees outside the section 5 tier hedging vested holdings with a bank product, on Compliance Certificate acknowledgement by the Group General Counsel within a 7-day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Woodside will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Restructuring a collar as a cash-settled swap, a funded forward or a family-trust transaction will be judged by economic effect against the derivatives, hedging and pledging bans.

bespoke_clauses.topic: arrangements forcing disposal within three months
bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where financing is allowed, a loan or collar whose default or physical settlement could force delivery of shares acquired within the last three months is itself prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A response would normally be expected within 24 hours ... Any such approval will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Where a dealing is permitted, execution and settlement of documentation must fit in a 7-day window from approval or acknowledgement, and the approval can be conditioned or revoked before dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If any clearance, approval or acknowledgment is required for a dealing under this Policy, the clearance, approval or acknowledgement will not be granted if the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hedge or financing by a senior person can be refused on perception grounds alone, without reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy extends to all securities owned or controlled by a person covered by the Policy, whether those securities are held in the name of that person, in a company, through a trust, by a family member, by a friend or in some other entity or arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Placing the collared shares in a trust, company or nominee does not take the collar or pledge outside the bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Debt transactions that may be converted into Woodside shares are also prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A financing structured as an exchangeable or convertible instrument over Woodside shares is caught for the section 5 tier.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for Woodside directors, executive key management personnel or other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan: section 5.1 expressly prohibits transactions in Woodside-based derivative securities including collars and writing puts or calls, whether for hedging or not and regardless of vesting state, and section 8.1 separately bans directors, Company Secretaries and CEO direct reports from pledging Woodside securities as collateral, with no exemption authority. The only potential candidates are restricted employees nominated by the Group General Counsel who are not executive incentive plan participants or CEO direct reports: for them an OTC hedge of a vested, unlocked holding and a secured loan are each dealings requiring a Compliance Certificate acknowledged by the GGC, executed within 7 days, outside the 31 December and 30 June black-out periods, passing the Front Page Test and not forcing disposal of shares acquired within three months. Ordinary employees may enter such arrangements without notification subject to the insider trading, Front Page Test and short-term dealing rules. A secured lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the Policy except for directors in a black-out period, and all approvals are discretionary, conditionable and revocable.
